key_insight: Q-DICE provides a hardware-aware compiler and emulator that lets researchers benchmark distributed quantum circuits realistically, even without access to distributed quantum hardware.
engineering_relevance: It helps co-design distributed quantum systems by enforcing topology and noise constraints during transpilation and simulation.
method: Constructs distributed QPU backends via QPU slicing and stitching.
Models nonlocal link noise with Kraus operators and stochastic error channels.
Uses a boundary-aware mapping algorithm to respect distributed topology constraints.
evidence_signal: The paper validates Q-DICE on multiple experimentally demonstrated circuits, including distributed Grover's search, and reports a worst-case fidelity deviation of 4% versus experimental results.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the chosen physical noise model and backend construction, so mismatches in link behavior or topology assumptions could limit realism.
paper_title: Q-DICE: Quantum Distributed Interconnect Compiler and Emulator
